bullets.title: CRM: Acquires Braze for $5.66B — Mixed Early Reaction, Antitrust Watch
bullets.body: Salesforce agreed to acquire Braze at $47.50/share (58-60% premium, ~$5.66B EV), valued at ~5-6x forward revenue on a ~$1B base growing 20%+ YoY. Deal closes in Salesforce FY28, funded entirely with cash (~4 months of FY27 FCF), no change to FY27 guidance or FY30 framework. Early buyside feedback described as mixed-to-negative; antitrust risk flagged given Braze lists CRM and ADBE as key competitors, with CRM IR head also departing. JPM maintains OW, Wolfe maintains OP at $360 PT, KeyBanc stays Sector Weight; CRM was down ~2.9% premarket.

bullets.title: NVDA: Hedgeye removes long, flags 80%+ of AI basket in bearish TREND; KOSPI -39% a warning sign
bullets.body: Hedgeye turned bearish on NVDA, noting 80%+ of 35 AI-theme stocks now signal bearish TREND and KOSPI has crashed 39.1% from peak — a leading semi indicator. Separately, MS TMT notes META's 1GW Prometheus supercluster in Ohio will use NVDA GB200/GB300 and upcoming Vera Rubin chips, and ByteDance/BABA/Tencent placed $35B+ in RTX PRO 5500 chip orders. AMZN power constraints are forcing NVDA racks into warehouses despite $5B+ August orders. Hedgeye's Keith McCullough sold all QQQ and is rotating into energy/DJIA.

bullets.title: Mag 7 AI Capex Buildout: AMZN, META, GOOGL, MSFT hyperscaler preview — buyside above consensus on all
bullets.body: MS TMT prime note: buyside expects AMZN Q3 AWS +44% YoY vs. consensus +38%, Q3 EBIT $28-29B vs. consensus $26B, and 2027 capex ~$350B vs. consensus $285B. META Q3 revenue expected $64B (+25% YoY high-end), 2027 capex $225-250B vs. consensus $201B. GOOGL Cloud +100% YoY expected in Q3 vs. consensus +90%, with TPU sales potentially $75-125B in 2027 — Mizuho's Klein says TPU revenue is significantly underestimated. MSFT F1Q27 Azure expected +47% YoY vs. guide high-end +44-55%. HF net Mag7 exposure at ~23% of US net, recently rotating from META/MSFT into GOOGL/NVDA.

bullets.title: WDC: UBS and MS both bullish into Q1 earnings (10/22); consensus expects $4.14B rev, $4.09 EPS
bullets.body: UBS models WDC Sept Q at $4.27B/$4.40 EPS well above Street; Dec Q at $5.03B/$5.93 vs. Street $4.56B/$4.78, with gross margins +550bps Q/Q to 63.5% on EB shipments +7% Q/Q and ASP +7% Q/Q. MS TMT names WDC a tactical long with preferred post-Q4 entry on asymmetrical setup; through-cycle HDD margins could hit 45-50%. Street consensus: $4.14B revenue, $4.09 EPS, 55.7% gross margin; options imply ~9.5% post-earnings move. Stock is up 32.2% since Aug 5; risk is Toshiba adding DC HDD capacity.

bullets.title: STX: Morgan Stanley reinstates as Top Pick on HDD upcycle; 80%+ upside in base case
bullets.body: MS TMT reinstated STX as Top Pick, citing Dec Q EPS 10-12% above consensus and 80%+ upside to base case, 100%+ in bull case, driven by the same enterprise HDD pricing and EB shipments tailwind supporting WDC. The thesis rests on through-cycle margin expansion in high-capacity nearline drives as AI-driven storage demand accelerates.

bullets.title: TXN: UBS expects high-end beat in CQ3; data center up 73-75% YoY; CQ4 guide above Street
bullets.body: UBS models TXN CQ3 revenue/EPS at high end of guidance ($6.05B/$2.48); CQ4 guidance expected $5.8-5.9B vs. Street ~$5.7B. Data center revenue growing 73%/75% YoY in CQ3/CQ4; analog buyers reportedly worried about supply shortages and pre-building. Wolfe also favors TXN as a beneficiary of competitor pricing increases without incurring higher costs. Key risk: personal electronics/handsets exposure (~17% of revenue) heading into Q4.

bullets.title: META: Prometheus 1GW supercluster confirmed with NVDA/AVGO/ANET/CRDO architecture; CPMs stepped up
bullets.body: MS TMT reports META's Prometheus cluster in Ohio will scale to ~1M GPUs using NVDA GB200/GB300 and Vera Rubin chips, with AVGO Jericho3, ANET 7800-series, and NVDA Spectrum-4 confirmed in the optical networking stack — CRDO also named as a beneficiary. Separately, Hedgeye notes META AI Muse US weekly users fell 42% within three weeks of launch, and META CPMs stepped up from early September though durability into 2027 is uncertain. Street 2027 capex consensus at ~$194B; Hedgeye sees no buy-side estimate above $250B.

bullets.title: NFLX: Bearish setup into earnings — engagement sliding, talent departing, trading 19x '27E
bullets.body: NFLX is down ~23% YTD and trading ~19x '27E. WSJ reports a streaming 'wall' as engagement slides to TikTok/YouTube; global Top-10 viewing hours fell 11% in Q3, and Netflix share of TV viewing dropped 1 point YoY in July. CCO, Head of Film, and Live Experiences executives departed alongside a ~1K layoff. 22V Research offers a contrarian trade: buy shares at $70 + sell Dec 65 put / 75 call strangle (7.2% yield, profitable $65-$80), citing P/E near 5-year lows at ~22x. Raymond James flags weak 3Q engagement data unlikely to clarify competitive position.

bullets.title: AAPL: Loop Capital downgrades to Hold, cuts PT to $330; iPhone Duo delivery dates moving forward
bullets.body: Loop Capital (analyst Ananda Baruah) downgraded AAPL from Buy to Hold, cutting PT from $370 to $330. Separately, MS TMT notes AAPL is moving iPhone Duo delivery dates forward and an Oct 28 event is expected to debut the first touchscreen MacBook and M6 14-inch MacBook Pro. MS views AAPL as a defensive FCF haven but questions remain on AI monetization.

bullets.title: GOOGL: De-rated on AI execution concerns; TPU upside underestimated; Search click-through falling
bullets.body: MS TMT notes GOOGL has been de-rated on AI execution risk; buyside expects Q3 Cloud +100% YoY vs. consensus +90%, but cautions on Agentic search disruption. Mizuho's Klein reiterates Outperform at $460 PT, arguing TPU revenue is 'significantly underestimated' in consensus and could reach $100B by 2028. On the negative side, Hedgeye reports Google search click-through fell in every agency benchmark segment in Q3, and Google AI Overviews now predominantly link to Reddit. GOOGL was down ~3% in recent trading vs. the sector.

bullets.title: EQIX: Morgan Stanley Top Pick on AI inferencing; Oppenheimer flags street estimates very low
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reaffirms EQIX as Overweight and Top Pick, co-hosting a Powering AI bus tour Nov 9-10 with management meetings at its 280 data centers across 77 markets. Oppenheimer separately notes EQIX has the best balance sheet and lowest/most accessible debt in the DC space, is the primary AI inference connection point, and that street estimates are 'very low' given AI application revenue growing better than expected. Near-term rate headwinds and equity supply from frontier IPOs are cited as risks to the entry point.

bullets.title: ANET: VAR checks solid (low-teens to ~30% YoY growth); benefits from META Prometheus architecture
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley 3Q VAR checks show ANET reseller growth ranging from low-teens to ~30% YoY, stronger in enterprise and financial services; pricing stability is supporting faster deal closures. ANET is also confirmed as part of META's Prometheus supercluster optical networking architecture (7800-series). CSCO showing stronger relative momentum at ~13% YoY with aggressive discounting to defend share.

bullets.title: ORCL: AI World preview (10/28) bullish — mgmt expected to raise FY30 $166B OCI target
bullets.body: Citi expects ORCL management to raise the FY30 $166B OCI revenue target at its Oct 28 AI World event, with improved EPS visibility driven by strong backlog. Analyst modestly raises ORCL FY28-29 Infrastructure revenue/EPS estimates; FY30 EPS est is 5%+ above consensus. ORCL is also collaborating with AstraZeneca on clinical trial optimization.

bullets.title: SPOT: Q3 setup flagged as 'interesting' on product launches; GS hosting earnings webinar
bullets.body: Raymond James flags SPOT as having an interesting Q3 setup given investment trajectory expected to translate into product launches, though no specific estimates are provided. GS is hosting a SPOT earnings recap webinar this week. No material negative signals in the checks.

bullets.title: TEAM: Citi raises PT to $245; Cloud beat >3% expected; FY27 ARR growth in 20s% achievable
bullets.body: Citi reaffirms Buy on TEAM (Atlassian) and raises PT to $245 from $225. F1Q27 Cloud revenue is expected to beat by more than 3%; Subs ARR growth in the 20s% is viewed as achievable with FY27 guidance likely guiding ~20%. Setup is described as demanding but medium-term conviction is strong.

bullets.title: MU: UBS BUY / $1,625 PT; Taiwan union strike Oct 22 a near-term watch item
bullets.body: UBS maintains BUY on MU with a $1,625 price target; a fireside chat with SVP Jeremy Werner on AI memory hierarchy is scheduled for Nov 9. Near-term risk: MU's Taiwan union plans a one-day strike on October 22 over an employee bonus dispute. Mizuho's Klein separately says China DRAM (CXMT) competitive threat is overblown given yield and performance gaps in server DRAM.

bullets.title: AMD: Substrate estimate correction flags prior overcount; Q4 accelerator business comfortable
bullets.body: Mizuho's Klein notes AMD's prior substrate estimate included ~1.4M Venice CPU units mistakenly categorized as GPU; October 2026 corrected estimate is 0.6M vs. July's 2.4M. Despite this, Wolfe views AMD as having Q4 accelerator upside driven by better TSMC 2nm capacity access, with $20 EPS near the street-high. GM weakness is already well-communicated.

bullets.title: EFX: UBS initiates Buy at $220 PT; stock +11% on Q3 beat and strong 2026 guidance
bullets.body: UBS initiates EFX at Buy with a $220 PT (11.3x 2028E EBITDA), citing differentiated data, government segment ACV reaching $550M YTD (vs. ~$300M prior), records growth accelerating to +12% YoY, and VantageScore mortgage lender adoption nearly doubling to ~2,000. Q3 EPS of $2.26 beat estimates; 2026 revenue guidance narrowed to $6.646-6.676B. Key risk: bimerge change could impact ~$80M revenue and ~$38M margin. JPM separately notes EFX's non-mortgage business alleviates AI-threat fears that had pressured info services stocks for 18 months.

bullets.title: TSLA: Earnings Wednesday — focus on Cybercab Austin deployment and FSD v15 autonomy signals
bullets.body: Oppenheimer previews TSLA earnings (Wednesday): focus on Cybercab Austin deployments and FSD v15 as the key autonomy read-through; aggressive capex and improving margins are expected. Morgan Stanley separately raised TSLA PT to $840 on autonomous vehicle upside per AlphaWise data.

bullets.title: CRWV / SMR / OKLO: Neoclouds and nuclear names broadly weak; SMR downgraded by Barclays
bullets.body: CRWV broke below July lows on massive volume (~100M shares), down ~20% in a week; premarket down another 4.9% as Korean neocloud provider Elice fell 32% on IPO debut, pressuring the complex. SMR was downgraded by Barclays and fell 7.6% premarket; OKLO down 3.7%. YTD: CRWV -57%, IREN -57%, SMR -87.5%, OKLO -83.3%. Hedgeye's Macro Show notes Constellation Energy and CoreWeave both failed to sustain headline-driven rallies.
